notes: For the coordinator. Two decisions are outstanding and neither is an implementer's. (1) **(a) is very likely a card defect, not a tree defect.** The page reports tauri=undefined and tauriInternals=object. Tauri v2 initialises its IPC bridge in every webview, so __TAURI_INTERNALS__ is injected regardless of configuration; withGlobalTauri:false governs __TAURI__ alone. C-BRIDGE@1 rule 4 forbids IPC *reachable from web content*, and "capabilities": [] (V3) is what makes it unreachable - the presence of the internals object is not itself a breach. The card's (a) demands something the stack does not provide; it was recorded as a FAIL with the observed value and NOT reinterpreted, and V3's greps were not offered as a substitute. Deciding whether (a) should assert reachability rather than the typeof of an always-injected global is a card amendment. (2) **The synthetic click does not land, and (b) and (c) are NOT RUN behind it.** The rect is published and correct (John Smith at 99,284) and the click uses the card's own xdotool mechanism, but nothing in the page changes within 30 s. The onboarding cause was found and fixed; the remaining cause is NOT established - a windowfocus hypothesis was tested and changed nothing, so it was reverted rather than left in as noise. Widening the 30 s timeout, accepting the enabled assertion as proof the click landed, or clicking until something changes are all forbidden here, so the row stays FAIL/NOT RUN. Three card observations are recorded rather than acted on: the producer re-fetches the pinned A06 revision because build-whisper-candidate.sh has no candidate-exists guard (the card's S0 text says otherwise); V0's own trap removes the build/linux-resources/web/dist it then requires, so a later release build must run the producer directly in front of tauri build; and V0's three 'run only if' predicates cannot see an unflagged shipped bundle. Nothing was weakened to reach any result: no count lowered, no assertion relaxed, no threshold moved, and both FAILs and both NOT RUNs are recorded as such.
